title: copilot-proxy-rs: many independent questions per request to the decision models
prompt:
The decision models gpt-6-luna-decisions (upstream /v1/decisions) and microsoft-decision-1 (upstream /v1/systemone) can answer many named questions in one upstream request, but clients can only reach them through chat routes (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses). There a prompt becomes either one yes/no question or a list of options whose probabilities are normalized to sum to 1. A client that needs several independent yes/no judgments (the software factory asks 4-20 per decision: gates, reviewer lenses, finding real/worth scores) must send one request per question. Measured: Jev (TypeSafe systemOne) answers 40 independent questions in one call in 0.08-0.42 s; the proxy models need 40 requests (2.7-3.6 s at copilot_max_rate=120) and each request uses a rate-limit token.

Goal: one proxy request carries many independent questions to either decision model, with the TypeSafe systemOne request and response shape, so a systemOne client can switch between Jev and these models by changing only the base URL and model.
1. Research first, with the existing Copilot auth on a branch build on 18080: the exact request and response shapes of upstream /v1/decisions and /v1/systemone for several questions in one request; which question types each supports (noul yes/no, choice with named criteria, score); limits on question count or size; error shapes. Compare with the TypeSafe systemOne API (request: {model, state, questions: {name: {type: noul|choice|score, instructions, criteria}}}; response: {answers: {name: {noul} | {choice, confidence, probabilities}}}; see the @typesafe-ai/sdk package or https://typesafe.ai docs if reachable). Record findings with sources in the PR body.
2. Add POST /v1/systemone on the proxy that accepts the systemOne request shape for model gpt-6-luna-decisions or microsoft-decision-1, sends ONE upstream request with all questions (translating to /v1/decisions for luna), and returns the systemOne response shape. noul is required; support choice if either upstream supports it natively, else answer choice by asking one predicate per criterion in the same upstream request and normalizing (document this). Unknown model or unsupported type: a clear 400. One rate-limit token per client request, not per question. Follow existing patterns in src/http and src/translate/decisions.rs; keep the chat routes unchanged.
3. GET /v1/models: list /v1/systemone in the decision models' supported endpoints so clients can find the route.
4. Tests: contract tests with recorded fixtures (synthetic values, real shapes) for both models: many noul questions, choice, mixed, unknown model, unsupported type, upstream error; no live calls in tests. cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked pass with no Cargo.lock change.
5. Proof on port 18080 (COPILOT_PROXY_RS_PORT=18080, COPILOT_PROXY_RS_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/copilot-proxy-rs so the existing config and token are read in place; never copy a token or config file, the shell refuses it): for each decision model, one POST /v1/systemone with 40 noul questions ("Is N a prime number?" for N=1..40) plus one choice question. Show in the PR body under "Proof": wall time, HTTP status, number of upstream requests and `rate limited` log lines for that one call, and how many of the 40 prime answers are correct (p >= 0.5 means yes). Compare with the old way (40 chat requests).
6. README: document the route with a curl example. PR body sections: Research, Proof, and "Client switch" showing the same request sent to Jev and to the proxy.
- Never touch, stop or bind the live proxy on 8080. Keep COPILOT_PROXY_RS_LOG_FAILED_REQUEST_BODIES behavior as is. Do not log tokens, prompts or bodies.
- This is a repeatable factory test: other open PRs for related work are earlier runs. Ignore them and build a new PR.
